tagline: Build things that work: apps, games, tools for your town.

modules.title: Your first program
modules.summary: Variables, text and numbers — and a program that talks back.
modules.task: Write a program that asks for your name and replies with a greeting and the number of letters in it.

test.q: What does print() do in Python?
options: Sends a document to the printer

modules.title: Decisions and loops
modules.summary: if, else and for — the building blocks of every game.
modules.task: Make a number-guessing game: the computer picks 1–100, you get hints “higher” or “lower”.

test.q: Which keyword repeats a block of code?

modules.title: Functions
modules.summary: Pack code into reusable pieces with a name.
modules.task: Write a function that converts złoty to euro and use it for three prices.

test.q: Why do we write functions?
options: To reuse code without copying it

modules.title: Data from the internet
modules.summary: Read JSON and show live information.
modules.task: Load the sample weather file for your town and print tomorrow's temperature.

test.q: What is JSON?

modules.title: Mini-project: town bus app
modules.summary: Put it all together in a tool people can use.
modules.task: Build a small app that shows the next bus from your stop. Share it in the live session.

test.q: What is the best first step in a project?
options: Plan the smallest version that works

tagline: Make technology clear, friendly and usable for everyone.

modules.title: Seeing like a designer
modules.summary: Hierarchy, contrast and spacing — why some screens feel easy.
modules.task: Take a photo of a school notice and redesign it so the key message is seen in 3 seconds.

test.q: What does visual hierarchy help with?
options: Showing what to look at first

modules.title: Colour and type
modules.summary: Pick colours and fonts with intention, not by luck.
modules.task: Create a 3-colour palette and 2 fonts for your town's football club and explain the choice.

test.q: Why check colour contrast?
options: So text is readable for everyone

modules.title: User research in 30 minutes
modules.summary: Ask good questions and listen.
modules.task: Interview three friends about how they check the bus timetable. Write down 3 problems.

test.q: A good interview question is…
options: “Tell me about the last time you…”

modules.title: Wireframes and prototypes
modules.summary: From paper sketches to a clickable mock-up.
modules.task: Sketch 3 screens of a timetable app on paper, then build a clickable prototype in a free tool.

test.q: What is a wireframe?
options: A simple sketch of a screen's layout

modules.title: Mini-project: a better town website
modules.summary: Research, design and test a real improvement.
modules.task: Redesign one page of your town's website and test it with two people. Present it in the live session.

test.q: Why test a design with real people?
options: To find problems you can't see yourself

tagline: Turn numbers into answers — and answers into decisions.

modules.title: Thinking in data
modules.summary: Questions first, numbers second.
modules.task: Write 5 questions about your school that data could answer. Pick the most interesting one.

test.q: What should come first in a data project?

modules.title: Spreadsheet superpowers
modules.summary: Sorting, filters and formulas that save hours.
modules.task: Collect your class's travel times to school and calculate the average and the longest trip.

test.q: What does an average tell you?

modules.title: Charts that tell the truth
modules.summary: Pick the right chart and avoid misleading ones.
modules.task: Make two charts from the same data: one honest, one misleading. Explain the trick.

test.q: A bar chart axis that doesn't start at zero can…

modules.title: Intro to SQL
modules.summary: Ask questions to a database.
modules.task: Use the sample town database to find the three busiest bus stops.

test.q: Which SQL word chooses columns?

modules.title: Mini-project: air in your town
modules.summary: A complete mini-analysis with open data.
modules.task: Analyse a month of open air-quality data for your region and present one finding in the live session.

test.q: A good data presentation ends with…

tagline: Understand AI, use it wisely and build your own small models.

modules.title: What AI really is
modules.summary: No magic: patterns, data and probability.
modules.task: List 5 AI tools you used this week without noticing. What data do they learn from?

test.q: Most AI systems learn from…

modules.title: Prompting well — and checking answers
modules.summary: Get better results and spot mistakes.
modules.task: Ask an AI chatbot three questions about your town's history and fact-check every answer.

test.q: What should you do with an AI answer?

modules.title: How machines learn
modules.summary: Training, testing and why data quality matters.
modules.task: Sort 20 photos into two groups by hand, then explain which rules you used — that's what a model learns.

test.q: Why split data into training and test sets?
options: To check the model on data it hasn't seen

modules.title: Train your first image classifier
modules.summary: No-code model training in your browser.
modules.task: Train a model in a free browser tool to tell apart two objects from your desk. Test it with a friend.

test.q: If your model often fails, what helps most?

modules.title: Mini-project: a responsible AI helper
modules.summary: Design an AI helper for your school — and think about fairness.
modules.task: Design an FAQ helper for your school. Write 3 rules to keep it fair and safe. Present it in the live session.

test.q: Why think about bias in AI?
options: Models can treat groups of people unfairly
